scope: E01-E25: estimator, confidence and output limitations; local planning only
execution_policy: Do not overwrite archived evidence, push, publish, send messages externally or upload project material. Fresh result directories only; toy/ledger/proof screens precede full financial execution. Existing solved mechanisms are reused without new speedup credit.

gate_definitions.G3: Explicit estimator schedule at 99% complete-price confidence

shared_rules: Status refers to the local subproblem or selected implementation, not a universal quantum advantage claim.
Current B4/B8 latest arithmetic source and archived C4/H8 compound-residual estimator are different workloads; do not cross-multiply favorable counts.
Finite-law digital mean certification and continuous-law financial price certification are separate interfaces.
Threshold epsilon, estimator dollar allowance and confidence split are frozen by G0/E07; saved residual e=0.002/discount and alpha=0.003 are defaults only for those saved contracts.
Query, arithmetic and physical costs must preserve the same source/inverse boundary; factored controls and fused graph cleanup are already paid optimizations.
Every scientific branch has a finite candidate budget and fallback; an unsuccessful local screen disproves only that candidate under its assumptions.
Multi-output, Greeks, infinite-variance and new nested-workload branches remain dormant unless their input/output contract is selected.

entries.title: Generic quadratic query scaling versus exploitable structure
entries.next_action: Write a one-page access-model card for the current single-price task, then select at most two structural escapes already proposed in the formulation plan. For each, enumerate the reduction from the actual finite source, source/inverse access, output normalization and preprocessing; reject an unbuilt price oracle before compilation.
alternatives: Restricted integration or analytically transformed payoff with an explicit reversible reduction.
Retain generic mean estimation and optimize its complete implementation; query optimality does not imply every structured financial problem is hard.
acceptance: The target price, digital law, epsilon and confidence remain identical, or a proved bias term is charged.
Every nontrivial oracle in the proposed reduction maps to existing emitted gates or a separately scoped implementation task.
A candidate advances only if its measured/source-manifest work product is strictly below the matched current quantum baseline; a theorem alone receives no speedup credit.
entries.stop_rule: Screen at most two transformations. Close this audit after their access-model cards; an absent implementable reduction leaves the generic estimator baseline in place, without a universal impossibility claim.
entries.on_pass: Queue the surviving transformation's smallest reversible predicate or preparation module in the formulation plan; send its declared estimator interface to E02.
entries.on_fail: Retain the current source-access model and continue exact arithmetic/certification work.

entries.title: Replace hypothetical k with executable source and inverse counts
entries.next_action: Implement a fresh read-only estimator ledger exporter. First expand one existing C4 Hadamard row and one C4 bounded row against their actual wrapper hashes; separately bind the selected B4/B8 financial output to a compatible estimator. Record fresh preparations, graph forwards/inverses, phase/selector forwards/inverses, reflection calls, longest chain, repetitions, rotations, measurement, reset and controller work.
alternatives: Explicit known-moment Hadamard tests when the identical digital second-moment certificate is available.
Exact shifted-selector bounded QAE as a moment-free finite-law fallback.
A separately certified iterative bounded-AE schedule from E04.
acceptance: Expanded gate multiplicities exactly reconcile to the emitted wrapper and integer schedule, with zero missing or duplicate routine calls.
Saved C4/H8 residual counts of 1,203,320/2,967,610 and bounded 7,864,305 are reproduced only for those saved residual contracts.
New B4/B8 costs use that workload's output, normalization, source hash and confidence schedule; C4/H8 calls are never multiplied by B4/B8 knock-out source depths.
An effective k may be reported only after deriving full counts; unsupported k=1 or k=3 remains a labelled sensitivity coordinate.
entries.stop_rule: Reconcile the two archived C4 rows and emit one selected estimator row per current financial source. Stop on any unexplained count/hash mismatch and repair accounting before another optimization branch.
entries.on_pass: Supply explicit invocation and chain counts to G3, E08, E20, E24 and the physical plan.
entries.on_fail: Mark the incompatible row invalid and rebuild that interface; preserve archived historical results.

entries.title: Match range or variance normalization to the actual amplitude oracle
entries.next_action: Produce an exact two-point digital-source example with one negative value. Execute the existing shifted selector and a small signed phase source on the same law; derive both dollar-error conversions and fully expand their source/inverse counts. Then attach the correct range or second-moment contract to every candidate ledger row.
alternatives: Bounded AE with p=E[(Y+128)/256], amplitude tolerance e/256 for the saved residual.
Signed phase estimation with a proved moment of the identical digital Y.
A tighter exact support range with a new selector and an all-input range proof.
acceptance: The selector's exact rational mean recovers Y's exact rational mean; signed-phase probabilities agree with the independent tiny-unitary calculation within 1e-12.
Discount and dollar scaling are explicit: the saved residual's undiscounted allowance is 0.002/discount, not an amplitude allowance.
No range-normalized count is replaced by sigma/e without changing and certifying its estimator/source pair.
entries.stop_rule: Test two tiny distributions, including a rare-event case, and the chosen current workload row. If normalization or moment provenance fails, discard that row and use the certified support fallback.
entries.on_pass: Freeze the chosen source-normalization contract for E04, E08 and E24.
entries.on_fail: Repair normalization first; do not spend on a full finance replay.

entries.title: Remove QFT/QPE only when the complete bounded-estimator schedule improves
entries.next_action: Implement a local modified-IQAE schedule/controller adapter around the unchanged selector, using the audited theorem and explicit round confidence. First cost its general bound at eta=(0.002/discount)/256 and alpha=0.003; next simulate exact tiny-source observation laws and retain only a finite certified schedule that improves the present bounded baseline.
alternatives: Modified IQAE without phase register/QFT.
Original IQAE with certified confidence intervals.
Retain canonical bounded QAE or the existing no-IQFT Hadamard method if costs are lower.
acceptance: A theorem-backed interval and stopping rule certify dollar error at most the selected e and estimator failure at most 0.003; all adaptive round decisions are covered.
Total forward/inverse calls, initial preparation per shot, deepest Q^m chain and paid feedback/readout are charged.
Promotion requires strictly less complete compiled work or supported complete latency than the same-output canonical baseline; deleting QFT alone does not pass.
The approximately 60,320,762*discount general query bound is labelled an upper-bound screen and never treated as a lower bound on IQAE.
entries.stop_rule: Cost three estimator families and at most eight preregistered controller settings on two exact toy laws. If no certified setting beats the baseline, close this branch and retain canonical/Hadamard estimation.
entries.on_pass: Emit the selected controller, integer schedule, exact confidence certificate and wrapper; update G3.
entries.on_fail: Keep the current certified bounded schedule and record why the candidate bound or executable schedule did not improve it.

entries.title: Factored external controls already avoid controlling every arithmetic gate
entries.next_action: Consume the existing controlled-conjugation proof and wrapper tests in the plan's accounting receipt. If a new estimator changes the wrapper, perform one tiny full-unitary comparison of direct control and A-controlled-S-A-inverse, including a superposed external control, reflection sign and clean scratch.
alternatives: Ordinary un-controlled Grover powers for iterative bounded AE.
Factored controlled reflection/conjugation for a controlled estimator.
acceptance: The changed tiny wrapper agrees as a full matrix to 1e-12, including relative phase rather than equality only up to global phase.
The zero-control branch is identity and workspace is restored on all toy basis states.
Current already-factored wrappers receive exactly zero new arithmetic speedup credit.
entries.stop_rule: No new experiment if wrapper semantics are unchanged. If changed, one exhaustive tiny-unitary regression closes the check; a phase mismatch blocks integration.
entries.on_pass: Reuse the existing factored wrapper in E02/G3 and proceed.
entries.on_fail: Correct control and reflection semantics before any source-cost comparison.

entries.title: Fused graph compute and uncompute is already implemented
entries.next_action: Audit each selected new wrapper's graph-half boundary: arithmetic forward, phase marking, arithmetic inverse, then reflection. Reuse archived fusion evidence; only run a tiny symbolic/gate comparison if a caller is still composing separately clean sources.
alternatives: Retain intermediates through phase kickback, then reverse once.
Use a separately clean source only when its external interface demands it.
acceptance: A fused wrapper has one graph forward and one graph inverse per marking operation, with the phase retained and scratch clean.
A real removed extra traversal is demonstrated from the caller expansion before claiming savings.
Existing fused callers receive zero additional gain; required coherent cleanup remains charged.
entries.stop_rule: Inspect the two selected estimator wrappers once. Close with no new gain if both already fuse; repair at most one demonstrated unfused caller and retest its interface.
entries.on_pass: Freeze correct graph-pass counts in E02 and leave storage/recomputation to the arithmetic/compiler plan.
entries.on_fail: Reject wrappers retaining garbage or double-counting source cleanup.

entries.title: One complete-price error and confidence ledger
entries.next_action: Create a rational ledger for one fixed price: deterministic law/tail/arithmetic/policy/surrogate/synthesis biases, statistical estimator failure, certificate-acquisition failures and physical execution failure. Map each term to a certificate or an explicitly open obligation; verify adaptive-stage failure allocation using exact fractions.
alternatives: Existing exact-binomial Hadamard confidence construction.
Certified iterative confidence intervals.
Canonical QAE with exact median-tail amplification.
acceptance: The sum of all deterministic dollar biases plus the estimator dollar-error allowance is at most the selected epsilon.
The sum of all failure allowances is at most 0.01; the saved residual estimator's allowance remains 0.003 unless a new complete ledger explicitly reallocates it.
A missing continuous-law, policy or physical certificate leaves complete-price status open; a 99% digital mean interval cannot close it.
Every chosen statistical event has a proved finite confidence bound; empirical agreement alone is not a certificate.
entries.stop_rule: One ledger per selected task, one reconciliation pass. Open terms become named prerequisite tasks; do not launch repeated estimation runs to conceal an unproved bridge.
entries.on_pass: Supply G2's error interfaces and G3's allowed estimator failure; unlock certified schedule comparisons.
entries.on_fail: Retain finite-law-only results and prioritize the first missing certificate.

entries.title: Further confidence allocation optimization against the already optimized schedule
entries.next_action: Hold the selected stage geometry and probability promises fixed. Search rational stage-failure allocations proportional to chain cost to powers 0, 1/2, 1 and 2, plus one discrete local optimization; recompute exact binomial thresholds and weighted call counts without using favorable observations.
alternatives: Current chain-proportional allocation, already implemented.
Uniform allocation as a diagnostic control.
Discrete budget allocation over existing certified stages.
acceptance: Exact rational small/large binomial tails sum to at most the allocated 0.003, with every adaptive interval transition covered.
The selected source and stage probability bounds remain unchanged.
An accepted setting has strictly fewer weighted controlled calls than the current optimized saved schedule; it is not compared only with the superseded billion-call schedule.
entries.stop_rule: Evaluate the five declared allocations and at most three local refinement rounds. No decrease or certificate failure retains the saved schedule.
entries.on_pass: Emit the new finite schedule and replace only its selected ledger row; feed G3.
entries.on_fail: Record that existing confidence allocation is adequate for this search and move on.

entries.title: Unknown variance without treating unknown sigma as an absolute-error certificate
entries.next_action: Write the audited unknown-variance/quantile algorithm as a complete finite controller for a bounded two-point source. Supply an absolute-dollar-error stopping/calibration rule, cap all stages, then enumerate quantile, centering, source and inverse calls for probabilities 1/2, 2^-8 and 2^-16.
alternatives: Quantum quantile and centering reductions from the audited unknown-variance theorem.
Analytic known-moment acquisition from E10.
Moment-free support-normalized estimation as a guaranteed fallback.
acceptance: No pilot variance or unobserved sample maximum is used as a certificate.
For all three exact laws, a finite theorem-backed procedure certifies error at most e and failure at most the chosen alpha, including calibration and stopping.
Coherent source and inverse access are explicit, and acquired classical data/certification costs are charged.
Only a complete acquisition-plus-estimation cost below the matched known-moment/support alternative advances to finance integration.
entries.stop_rule: One fully specified theorem variant and the three rare-event laws; allow at most two stopping-rule revisions. If only a fixed-n sigma/n guarantee is obtained, stop and keep this finance branch conditional.
entries.on_pass: Compile one small quantile primitive and compare complete work before attempting a full financial source.
entries.on_fail: Use E10 or bounded estimation; do not conclude unknown-variance quantum estimation is impossible.

entries.title: Acquire analytic moment bounds with outward rounding
entries.next_action: Implement interval evaluation of the existing C4 global fallback 2*q^2*E[(A-G)^2], using absolute future dates and the same continuous policy derivation. Measure bound acquisition time, evaluate the known-moment schedule using the outward bound, and keep the finite-source transfer obligation explicit.
alternatives: Global analytic AM-GM spread-moment fallback.
Conditional analytic parity/truncated-lognormal bounds with interval arithmetic.
Proved support bound when an analytic digital transfer is unavailable.
acceptance: Interval enclosures prove a nonnegative moment upper bound; cancellation and transcendental rounding are controlled.
Dates, covariance, payoff cap and policy match the continuous derivation exactly.
Total acquisition-plus-estimation work is compared with the saved pilot and support alternatives, rather than declaring a tighter moment free.
The result is labelled continuous-law conditional until E11 proves the identical digital moment; it cannot yet certify the compiled source.
entries.stop_rule: Evaluate C4 at 80 and 160 interval digits, then one H8 transfer of the implementation. If enclosure widths remain too loose after these two precisions or total work is worse, retain the support bound.
entries.on_pass: Pass the analytic upper moment and its law/policy contract to E11; use it only in conditional schedule screens meanwhile.
entries.on_fail: Archive the loose/expensive bound and choose the rigorous finite-source support fallback.

entries.title: Transfer second moments to the identical finite source with an L2 bridge
entries.next_action: First prove one all-input/tail-controlled L2 error bound for the finite midpoint transform on a scalar smooth capped payoff. Propagate it through guarded path arithmetic, then isolate the exercise-policy indicator as a separate boundary term. Derive sqrt(E[Y_d^2]) <= sqrt(E[Y^2])+b only for the identical policy/law coupling.
alternatives: L2 coupling from the continuous law and outward analytic moments.
Direct digital moment upper bounds by exact finite sums on a restricted toy and rigorously bounded production integration.
Unconditional signed-support bound with no tight-moment transfer.
acceptance: Each bound controls all source words plus the excluded continuous tails; sampled maxima are diagnostics only.
The source guard, clipping and policy are included; analytic Gaussian control expectations are not assumed exact under finite Box-Muller draws.
Minkowski uses a proved L2 b, not merely an L1 price-error allowance.
A tight moment advances only when its complete certificate applies to the same Y_d hash and lowers certified estimator work relative to the support bound.
entries.stop_rule: Three scoped proofs: scalar transform, smooth path/payoff, policy-boundary term. If a proof fails, document the exact missing inequality and retain the support estimator; no unbounded sampled search.
entries.on_pass: Attach the digital moment certificate to G2/E03 and re-cost the selected Hadamard schedule.
entries.on_fail: Keep continuous moments as conditional evidence and continue with the rigorous bounded estimator.

entries.title: Anytime-valid statistical moment acquisition
entries.next_action: Implement the audited bounded empirical-Bernstein confidence sequence for independent outer-group squared residual observations. Compare its declared stopping rule with fixed-N acquisition on exact rare-event laws at p=1/2, 2^-8 and 2^-16, then run one eligible finance acquisition only if the toy design and theorem assumptions pass.
alternatives: Anytime-valid confidence sequence.
Existing fixed-N iid certificate.
Analytic moment or support fallback, which needs no stochastic pilot.
acceptance: Conditional-mean/independence and bounded-range hypotheses are documented; individual dependent Sobol points are not passed off as iid.
The proof covers optional stopping and all looks, at the same allocated acquisition failure.
Zero observations still give the nonzero range/tail term prescribed by the bound.
Promotion requires smaller complete acquisition-plus-estimation latency for the selected finance task; empirical coverage simulation is only a diagnostic.
entries.stop_rule: Three toy laws and at most one finance acquisition with a preregistered sample/time cap no larger than the fixed-N baseline. On cap exhaustion use the fallback, not repeated uncorrected looks.
entries.on_pass: Export the stopping certificate and acquisition cost to E07/E02.
entries.on_fail: Use the fixed-N, analytic or support certificate and record that this acquisition design did not help.

entries.title: Exact uniform-selector payoff loading is already implemented
entries.next_action: Reuse the existing shifted_selector and its exhaustive small truth tables. For each newly selected output, prove its exact signed support, choose the selector span, bind its real output address and include selector random bits in reflection; rerun boundary/inverse checks only when span or binding changes.
alternatives: Existing exact signed shifted-uniform comparator.
A newly proved smaller power-of-two support span.
Synthesized amplitude loading only if it demonstrably reduces full work after its approximation error is charged.
acceptance: Exact selector probability equals the shifted fixed-point payoff for every toy input and at production signed boundaries.
Both flag inputs, nonzero outputs, comparator cleanup and inverse restoration pass.
The reflected state includes all financial-random and selector bits.
The saved span-256 loader receives zero new credit; new support tightening needs an all-input proof.
entries.stop_rule: No reinvention of the existing loader. One changed-binding/changed-span verification closes integration; failed range proof returns to the existing safe span.
entries.on_pass: Bind the reused loader into E02/E04 and G3.
entries.on_fail: Reject unsafe support assumptions or incomplete reflection; restore the validated selector.

entries.title: Replace prohibitive nested constants only with an explicit coherent schedule
entries.next_action: Instantiate one audited repeatedly-nested estimator at D=1 on a two-point bounded transition and a declared Lipschitz outer payoff. Build its deterministic level schedule, finite constants and coherent wrapper; compare integer conditional-source calls with the saved bounded-inner/signed-outer hierarchy at three error targets.
alternatives: Deterministic level scheduling from the audited nested-estimation theorem.
The existing explicit bounded-inner hierarchy as a control.
Flattening with certified same-policy baseline and regret, when the contract supports it.
acceptance: Both methods target the same exact nested expectation and error/failure allocation.
Function evaluation and each trajectory/source/inverse step are charged using emitted toy gates, even if abstract theorem cost sets them to zero.
Constants, maximum level, repetitions and coherent inner output format are explicit.
Advance only if conditional-source calls or complete compiled work strictly decrease at at least one same-contract target; fixed-D asymptotics are not an implemented speedup.
entries.stop_rule: One theorem variant, D=1, three error targets and at most two schedule refinements. No improvement keeps the current hierarchy or selects a separately certified flattening branch.
entries.on_pass: Use E15 to validate the coherent interface before any finance compiler integration.
entries.on_fail: Archive a finite negative screen; do not treat the saved 1.1e15–4.9e16 calls as a universal nesting lower bound.

entries.title: Measured adaptive inner estimation is not a coherent outer oracle
entries.next_action: Build a two-outer-state toy coherent inner computation, apply its outer payoff, then reverse. For each candidate inner estimator, choose a reversible fixed schedule or explicitly store and uncompute the control/measurement records; separately inventory the flattening baseline and regret certificates.
alternatives: Fixed coherent inner schedule and coherent median.
Deferred measurement with stored records, padded branches and reversible controller, charged in full.
Certified policy-residual flattening with its nonnegative regret term retained.
acceptance: The tiny outer-state superposition preserves intended coherence and all scratch is restored; full unitary error is at most 1e-12.
The estimator's approximate inner output error is included in the outer dollar budget.
Measured IQAE results for separately sampled outer states are never labelled a reversible coherent source.
Flattening is accepted only for the identical digital policy with proved baseline, residual and regret accounting.
entries.stop_rule: Compare at most two coherent toy designs and the existing flattening interface. If records/padding erase the expected benefit or cleanup fails, keep the fixed schedule/flattening fallback.
entries.on_pass: Supply the verified unitary interface to E14 and the formulation plan.
entries.on_fail: Reject the incompatible measured-inner design before pricing compilation.

entries.title: Finite-variance heavy tails have query alternatives with explicit bias and weights
entries.next_action: For one exactly evaluable scalar lognormal payoff, derive a rigorous second moment and dollar tail-cap bias. Cost three finite constructions: capped bounded AE, quantile finite-variance estimation and one analytically weighted change of measure. Separate full payoff tails from the already bounded parity residual.
alternatives: Proved clipping/tail cap with bounded AE.
Quantile finite-variance estimator with explicit finite source.
Analytic change of measure including its likelihood-ratio weights.
acceptance: Finite second moment and finite-law bias are proved for the actual weighted payoff, not for an unweighted pilot.
Tail bias plus discretization/arithmetic bias plus estimation error is at most the selected dollar epsilon.
Preparation, likelihood arithmetic, quantile calls and inverses appear in the complete ledger.
A candidate advances only with lower complete work than the best same-law quantum construction and the scalar classical comparator is given the same transform.
entries.stop_rule: One scalar payoff and the three declared constructions at two epsilon targets. Failure of moment/bias certification rejects that construction; no multi-asset compilation until a candidate passes.
entries.on_pass: Send the smallest certified tail/source module to the formulation plan and E02.
entries.on_fail: Retain a certified capped/support construction and leave the theorem-level escape conditional.

entries.title: Infinite variance and undefined mean require different contracts
entries.next_action: Audit whether any selected pricing workload actually lacks a finite second moment. Current finite-source/clipped residuals and ordinary finite-parameter GBM do not activate this branch. If a future finite-mean heavy-tailed contract does, use one Pareto toy with a proved pth moment for 1<p<2 and derive a clipping budget before comparing an Lp estimator with a robust classical method.
alternatives: Lp quantum integration/mean estimation with a fully declared oracle and moment bound.
Clipping at B with bias at most M_p/B^(p-1).
Decline an undefined-price mean rather than misclassifying it as a quantum complexity obstruction.
acceptance: The actual selected workload's moment status is proved or explicitly unknown; an unrelated heavy-tail toy does not become evidence against GBM.
If activated, B follows from a proved population pth moment and the dollar bias budget, never the observed sample maximum.
Quantum and robust classical methods share the same finite-mean target, finite precision, epsilon and failure standard.
entries.stop_rule: One workload relevance audit closes this point. Run at most one Pareto construction only when G0 selects such a contract; otherwise mark not applicable to the current single-price program.
entries.on_pass: Activate a separately scoped Lp/tail module if relevance is established; otherwise keep this point audited and dormant.
entries.on_fail: If the mean diverges, document that the price is undefined under that model; if only the proof is missing, preserve uncertainty.

entries.title: Multi-output tasks need their own norm, confidence and access contract
entries.next_action: Keep the current one-price output fixed. If G0 later activates multiple outputs, use three strikes on a shared exact toy distribution to compare separate AE, a requested scalar weighted portfolio and a common output basis under explicitly distinct contracts; charge simultaneous confidence and reconstruction error.
alternatives: Separate certified scalar estimates.
One scalar portfolio estimator when that is the requested output.
Multivariate or low-rank output basis with a proved reconstruction bound.
acceptance: For an actual three-price task, every component meets the same declared dollar tolerance and simultaneous failure is at most 0.01.
A weighted portfolio scalar is never substituted for separately requested prices.
Dimension, covariance/norm and parameterized oracle costs are explicit; no automatic sqrt(K) overhead claim.
The classical comparator shares paths, covariance information and any usable basis.
entries.stop_rule: Dormant while G0 requests one price. If activated, three output contracts and one exact toy comparison; reject empirical-only low-rank reconstruction and stop before finance compilation.
entries.on_pass: Create a separately versioned multi-output contract and ledger; advance only a certified improving design.
entries.on_fail: Retain scalar estimation or the existing one-price task, without universal dimension claims.

entries.title: Quantum Greeks must compete with classical adjoint differentiation
entries.next_action: Keep this branch dormant for a one-price task. If Greeks are requested, specify a smooth two-parameter payoff with analytic sensitivities, compile a parameter-superposition oracle and compare its gradient schedule with reverse-mode pathwise differentiation using the same paths; isolate barrier smoothing and its bias separately.
alternatives: Coherent quantum gradient estimation from an explicit parameterized oracle.
Shared-path classical reverse-mode/pathwise adjoints.
Finite differences only as a diagnostic control, not the strongest classical comparator.
acceptance: Price and each sensitivity have declared units, bias allowances, absolute-error targets and simultaneous confidence.
The parameter-superposition oracle and inverse are emitted and synthesis costs counted.
Nonsmooth/barrier derivatives require a proved smoothing or likelihood/pathwise justification.
Promotion requires lower complete latency/work against the matched classical adjoint construction, not K independent classical price runs.
entries.stop_rule: Dormant until G0 changes the deliverable. If activated, one smooth toy and one quantum/adjoint comparison; no barrier finance implementation without a derivative-bias proof.
entries.on_pass: Open a separately versioned sensitivity program with its own matched comparator.
entries.on_fail: Retain classical adjoints for requested sensitivities and preserve the original single-price program.

entries.title: Entangled parallel AE must pay for all source lanes and physical scheduling
entries.next_action: Specify one audited entangled parallel-AE construction at P=1,2,4 using one fixed compatible source and alpha allocation. Emit the finite query/chain/QSP/GHZ schedule and lane memory. Send those rows to the physical plan for routing/factory/data-memory timing under one stated qubit budget; first reject rows whose bare lane memory already exceeds that budget.
alternatives: Entangled parallel AE with GHZ/QSP.
Independent repetitions or shallow estimators, costed as different algorithms.
Serial selected estimator with compiler-level parallel arithmetic.
acceptance: Each lane pays for its complete source workspace; lane, GHZ, QSP, rotation and readout memory/resources are all included.
Confidence conversion follows E21; an RMSE-only row cannot satisfy G3.
Complete paid latency is compared under the same physical budget, including factories and routing; serial time/P with one source's memory fails.
Advance only if at least one valid P row strictly reduces complete latency; a necessary capacity screen alone is insufficient.
entries.stop_rule: Evaluate exactly P=1,2,4 for one source and one architecture. Stop at the first impossible memory cap or after all rows; expand P only if a valid best row and explicit budget headroom justify one further finite sweep.
entries.on_pass: Deliver the selected finite schedule to G3 and the physical G5 gate.
entries.on_fail: Use serial/shallow estimation; retain the parallel theorem as a conditional depth tradeoff.

entries.title: Convert RMSE to the allocated high-probability dollar guarantee
entries.next_action: Implement a read-only confidence converter for every RMSE-based candidate. Compare one run with RMSE<=e*sqrt(alpha) against a finite odd median of independent runs each with RMSE<=e/2; use exact binomial tails for the latter. Apply both to E20's finite P rows before physical promotion.
alternatives: Squared-error Markov conversion for one run.
Independent median amplification with exact rational tail upper bounds.
A separately proved direct high-probability estimator theorem.
acceptance: For alpha=0.003, every retained schedule has a proved Pr(abs(error)>e)<=0.003, after normalization and discount.
The one-run target is e*sqrt(0.003), not merely RMSE=e; a total 99% conversion e/10 cannot silently replace the smaller estimator allocation.
Median runs charge every source/inverse/preparation/readout and any lane reset.
Select the lower valid complete work/latency conversion; all direct high-probability assumptions are explicit.
entries.stop_rule: Evaluate the two elementary conversions and at most one audited direct theorem; no numerical coverage-only substitution.
entries.on_pass: Attach the finite confidence schedule to the relevant E20/E02 row and G3.
entries.on_fail: Reject RMSE-only candidates from the 99% price comparison.

entries.title: Classify actual payoff predicates before importing log-domain QSP
entries.next_action: Export every current barrier, exercise and payoff predicate from the target IR into a classification table: one-asset monotone threshold, min/max, sum of prices, arithmetic average or other. Prove any one-asset log-domain replacement on its entire supported domain; build only that small predicate before proposing a QSP source replacement.
alternatives: Exact monotone one-asset log predicate where the contract permits it.
Min/max predicates built from certified component tests.
Retain arithmetic for sums/averages of exponentials or seek a separately certified structured approximation.
acceptance: Every selected source predicate appears once in the classification table with an IR identifier and domain.
An exact replacement preserves every digital predicate input, including threshold ties, guarded endpoints and signed rounding.
A sum-of-asset-prices barrier is never identified with a threshold on one log return.
Current basket/average semantics remain unchanged; the cited autocallable's 68%/one-second comparison is not used as this project's advantage claim.
entries.stop_rule: One complete predicate census and at most two algebraically eligible predicate proofs. If no predicate is eligible, close exact log-domain transfer without attempting a full arithmetic-free source.
entries.on_pass: Compile the smallest exact predicate, measure its emitted work and send any approximate amplitude factor to E23.
entries.on_fail: Keep arithmetic predicates and pursue exact arithmetic or a new separately labelled financial workload only through G0.

entries.title: QSP approximation, rotation synthesis and dollar bias are one budget
entries.next_action: For one eligible bounded scalar payoff factor, freeze its signal encoding and approximation interval. Search degrees 8,16,32,64; use interval extrema to certify polynomial-amplitude error, then allocate synthesis operator error over all QSP invocations and estimator repetitions and emit the selected finite signal/QSP schedule.
alternatives: Certified QSP approximation with explicit signal preparation.
Current exact/deterministic register arithmetic.
A different encoding or interval only as a separately budgeted second candidate.
acceptance: Uniform amplitude error b is proved on the full certified interval and its dollar probability error includes b*(abs(p)+abs(f)) times normalization, plus tails/domain exclusions.
Each signal-oracle use, repeated state preparation, rotation sequence and inverse is charged.
Synthesis operator error is allocated over the complete estimator invocation count; single-module error alone is insufficient.
Promotion requires smaller source-plus-QSP compiled work or supported latency at the same total dollar bias than the emitted arithmetic module.
entries.stop_rule: Four declared degrees and at most two encodings on one factor. If no fully certified candidate beats arithmetic, keep the arithmetic leaf; do not raise degree indefinitely.
entries.on_pass: Integrate one factor with fresh wrapper/error manifests, update G2/G3, then compare complete sources.
entries.on_fail: Retain the arithmetic implementation and document whether degree, preparation or synthesis dominated.

entries.title: Optimize the error split only over supported certificates
entries.next_action: Collect existing certified precision/law/arithmetic rows without rerunning finance. Enumerate only represented word widths and statistical-error fractions 0.25,0.45,0.65 of the selected epsilon; keep failure budgets separate. Recompute source/estimator/synthesis cost for each feasible ledger, then request only the smallest missing certificate needed by a promising row.
alternatives: Current e=0.45*epsilon split.
More statistical allowance with a cheaper certified source where deterministic bias permits it.
Tighter arithmetic/law allowance when it decreases estimator repetitions enough to justify its cost.
acceptance: All retained deterministic-bias bounds plus estimator error sum to at most epsilon and all failure allowances sum to at most 0.01.
Every feasible row cites a certificate valid at its exact word width, source law and policy; unsupported interpolation fails.
The selected row has strictly lower complete compiled work or supported latency than the current same-task ledger.
Incomplete certificates produce conditional screens and never a G2 pass; deleted/unused error terms are explicitly reallocated.
entries.stop_rule: One finite grid of existing certified widths times three error fractions, followed by at most one newly justified precision certificate. If all rows are infeasible or worse, retain the original split.
entries.on_pass: Freeze the chosen complete ledger and regenerate G3/physical inputs without changing the financial task.
entries.on_fail: Keep the current allocation and prioritize named missing certificates rather than repeated source sweeps.

entries.title: Adaptive Bayesian/likelihood designs need a coverage proof
entries.next_action: First inspect the complete primary derivation for one Bayesian or likelihood design, using public read-only research access without uploading project material. Reproduce its finite design on an exact small-amplitude grid plus near-alias points; wrap adaptive selection in a proved frequentist stopping interval or reject it from the current guarantee. Keep device-noise and prior assumptions explicit.
alternatives: Bayesian design selection with a separate valid confidence sequence/test wrapper.
Maximum-likelihood experiment selection with a uniform coverage certificate.
Current exact-binomial or certified iterative estimator as fallback.
acceptance: The selected stopping interval has proved coverage at the allocated alpha for all allowed amplitudes, including aliasing boundaries and adaptivity.
Posterior credibility alone and simulated average coverage do not close the 99% requirement.
Noise calibration, priors, failed shots, design/controller work and paid readout are charged under a declared model.
Promotion requires lower full certified work/latency than the strongest existing valid schedule for the same source.
entries.stop_rule: One fully read primary design, one bounded exact-law diagnostic grid and at most one coverage-wrapper construction. Without a coverage proof or an improvement, stop this branch and preserve the valid baseline.
entries.on_pass: Emit a fresh finite confidence and cost certificate; update only its compatible estimator row.
entries.on_fail: Retain the Bayesian/likelihood design as a research lead and use the certified current estimator.
